title: Let Him Who Is Without Sin
text:
Early one morning Jesus was teaching in the Temple courts when the scribes and Pharisees brought in a woman who had been caught in adultery. They made her stand before everyone. "Teacher," they said, "this woman was caught in the act. In the law Moses commanded us to stone such women. What do you say?" They were setting a trap: whatever he answered could be used against him.

Jesus bent down and began to write on the ground with his finger. They kept pressing him for an answer. At last he straightened up and said, "Let any one of you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone at her." Then he bent down again and went on writing.

One by one the accusers went away, beginning with the eldest, until Jesus was left alone with the woman standing there.

He looked up and asked her, "Woman, where are they? Has no one condemned you?" "No one, sir," she said. "Neither do I condemn you," Jesus answered. "Go, and from now on do not sin again."
lesson: Before you condemn someone, take an honest look at your own record. You can hold a high standard and still offer people a way forward.
people: Jesus, a woman, scribes and Pharisees
caveat: The passage is missing from the earliest surviving manuscripts of John and is widely thought to be a later insertion of an older tradition.
